title: Finance Content Studio India: Whiteboard & Screen-Record Setup

children.text: A practical look at what finance and edtech content creators actually need from a studio in India — whiteboard sessions, screen-record videos, and the disclosure basics worth sorting out before the shoot.

layout.content: Finance Content Studio India: Whiteboard & Screen-Record Setup

If you make finance or edtech videos — stock market explainers, mutual fund breakdowns, personal finance Q&As — the biggest production decision isn't your camera, it's finding the right finance content studio in India. Most of these videos split into two formats: whiteboard explainers, where you talk while sketching a concept, and screen-record videos, where your voice sits over a trading app, a spreadsheet, or a slide deck. Each format needs a different room setup, and booking the wrong one wastes a shoot day. This guide walks through what to look for, what it costs by the hour in Delhi NCR, Gurugram and Noida, and the disclosure checklist finance creators in India now have to run before they hit record.
What a Finance Content Studio Actually Needs

General-purpose photography and reels studios are built around backdrops, ring lights and props, not around a clean monitor feed or a wall big enough to sketch a compound-interest chart on. A studio that works for finance and edtech content usually has three things a standard studio skips: a clean HDMI or capture-card feed from a laptop to a recording rig, a plain wall or actual whiteboard with even lighting so there are no hotspots that wash out marker lines, and a quiet room, because a 12-minute explainer on mutual fund taxation has nowhere to hide traffic noise the way a 30-second reel does. Before booking, ask the host directly whether the room has a dedicated capture setup. Plenty of "content studios" in Delhi NCR are optimised for fashion and product shoots and will need extra gear, and extra time, to support a screen-record session.
Whiteboard Setup vs Screen-Record Setup
These are two different shoots, and mixing them into one hour-long slot usually means neither comes out clean.

A whiteboard session needs a large whiteboard or painted wall, a tripod positioned to the side so your hand doesn't block the frame, warm even lighting across the whole board, and markers in at least two colours, since most presenters alternate colours for emphasis. Budget 10-15 minutes of setup per topic change if you're recording multiple explainers back-to-back, because re-centering the board and wiping old diagrams eats time.

A screen-record session needs a laptop-to-studio HDMI or USB-C capture connection, a second monitor so you can see your own feed while narrating over a chart or a trading app, a lavalier or shotgun mic routed into the house audio interface rather than your laptop's built-in mic, and a simple desk or standing setup framed from the chest up. Most hosts can manage this with 15-20 minutes of setup if you tell them in advance. Walking in and asking for a capture card on the spot is the single most common reason finance shoots run over their booked slot.
Book 30 extra minutes on top of your expected shoot length for a first finance content session — setup and test-recording for screen capture almost always takes longer than creators budget for.
Camera, Audio and Lighting for Charts and Numbers
Numbers and small text are unforgiving on camera. A few things matter more here than in a typical reel shoot.

items: Shoot whiteboard sections at a slight downward or side angle to avoid glare bouncing off marker ink under softbox lights.
For screen-record, confirm the studio's output resolution matches your source — recording a 1080p slide deck through a lower-resolution capture card makes text blurry on playback.
Clip a lav mic close to the collar. Finance explainers often run 8-15 minutes, and room-mic audio noticeably degrades over that length as presenters move around.

If you're alternating between whiteboard and screen segments in one session, ask the host to save two lighting presets in advance rather than re-lighting between takes. This alone can save 20-30 minutes on a half-day shoot.

layout.content: Typical Pricing for a Finance Content Studio in India

Pricing for a finance content studio in India tracks closer to a standard talking-head or podcast studio than a full production set, since the core requirement is a clean feed rather than elaborate styling. Across Delhi, Gurugram and Noida, expect roughly ₹1,200-₹2,500 per hour for a basic whiteboard or single-camera screen-record room with a 2-hour minimum booking, and ₹2,500-₹4,500 per hour for a studio with a dedicated capture rig, a second monitor, and multi-mic support for interview-style finance content. Hourly rates typically drop 10-20% for half-day (4+ hour) bookings, which matters if you're batching 3-4 explainer videos in one visit, a common pattern for weekly finance YouTube channels trying to stay ahead on their content calendar.
Disclosure Checklist Before You Hit Record

Finance content in India carries a regulatory layer that a cooking or fashion shoot doesn't. SEBI's rules on who can discuss stocks, mutual funds and investment strategy online have tightened over the past couple of years, and the practical upshot for a studio booking is simple: plan your disclosures and disclaimers before the camera rolls, not in post-production.

items: If you're a registered investment adviser, research analyst, or distributor, plan on-screen time for your registration number and grievance contact details rather than relying on a caption below the video.

If you're an educational creator who isn't registered and isn't giving personalised advice, keep the framing clearly educational and avoid language that reads as a specific buy or sell recommendation.
Script the disclaimer as a spoken line and an on-screen graphic together, rather than one or the other. Current guidance favours disclosures that are hard to miss, not fine print.

Check the latest SEBI circulars on finfluencer conduct before each new content format, since live streams, shorts and long-form explainers are increasingly treated differently and this is an area that keeps evolving.

layout.content: None of this changes the studio booking itself, but it does change your shot list. Leave room in your schedule for a disclosure slide or a spoken intro line on every video, not just the first one.
Booking Checklist: What to Confirm Before the Shoot

items: Confirm the room has a working HDMI or USB-C capture path to a recording device, tested before your slot rather than during it.
Ask whether a second monitor or confidence screen is included, or whether you need to bring your own.
Clarify whether lav mics are included in the base rate or charged separately.
Check the whiteboard size against your content. A compound-interest chart needs more real estate than a quick two-line note.
Ask for a 15-20 minute buffer before your booked slot if this is your first screen-record session at that studio.

layout.content: FAQs: Finance Content Studios in India
What's the difference between a whiteboard studio and a regular content studio?

A regular content studio is set up for backdrops, props and ring-light portraits. A whiteboard studio adds a large writing surface with even, glare-free lighting and a tripod angle that keeps your hand out of frame, features a standard reels studio usually doesn't have ready without extra setup time.
Can I record screen-capture finance videos without my own capture card?

Many studios in Delhi NCR that cater to edtech and finance creators now carry an HDMI or USB-C capture setup as part of the room, but it isn't universal. Always confirm this with the host before booking rather than assuming it, since bringing your own card on the day adds setup time you may not have budgeted for.
How long should I book for a finance explainer video shoot?

For a single 8-12 minute explainer, book at least 90 minutes to allow for lighting checks, a test recording, and 2-3 takes. If you're batching multiple topics in one session, add 15-20 minutes per topic for whiteboard resets or screen-source changes.
Do I need to show disclosures on screen, or is a caption enough?

Current SEBI guidance for finfluencers and registered advisors favours disclosures that are visible and spoken, not buried in a caption. Plan this into your shot list as its own few seconds of screen time rather than treating it as an afterthought.
What audio setup works best for finance explainers?

A lavalier mic routed through the studio's audio interface outperforms a room or laptop mic for anything over five minutes, since finance explainers involve more pauses and tonal shifts than a quick reel, and room-mic audio tends to pick up more ambient noise over a longer take.

Final takeaways

Finance and edtech content needs a studio that's set up for clean capture and legible detail, not just good lighting for a face. Get the room specs right before you book, and build your disclosure checklist into the shoot itself rather than fixing it in editing.

items: Confirm the studio has a tested HDMI or USB-C capture path before booking a screen-record session.
Book extra buffer time of 30 minutes or more for your first session in a new finance content studio.
